a.summary: Git auto-merged main's new 4th constructor argument `serializedSignatureCount` into every call site, but the sibling file `TransactionSkeletonImpl.java` on the v1_tx side has no such parameter — its constructor is `(data, version, messageOffset, numSignatures, numReadonlySignedAccounts, ...)`. As written this file does not compile, and the tempting local "fix" (deleting the argument here) would silently discard main's commit 7377486: `requireSignableSignatureLayout()` rejects a serialized signature-slot count that disagrees with the message header's required-signature count, and a signature-count prefix longer than one byte, before any `createTransaction` builds a mutable `TransactionRecord`. Dropping the argument also invalidates the `@throws IllegalStateException` Javadoc that hunks 2 and 7 keep on the three abstract `createTransaction` declarations.

b.summary: CONFIRMED by inspection of the sibling working-tree file. Git auto-merged main's new 4th constructor argument `serializedSignatureCount` into every call site, but on the v1_tx side of `TransactionSkeletonImpl.java` the constructor (working-tree lines 47-62) is `(byte[] data, int version, int messageOffset, int numSignatures, int numReadonlySignedAccounts, int numReadonlyUnsignedAccounts, int numIncludedAccounts, int accountsOffset, int recentBlockHashIndex, int numInstructions, int instructionsOffset, int[] invokedIndexes, int lookupTablesOffset, PublicKey[] lookupTableAccounts, int numAccounts)` — no `serializedSignatureCount`. Both the record component `int serializedSignatureCount` and the whole `private void requireSignableSignatureLayout()` body live ONLY inside HEAD-side conflict blocks of that file (lines 24-40 and 470-510 respectively), so a naive 'take theirs' there silently deletes main's 7377486 hardening. As written this file does not compile, and the tempting local 'fix' (deleting the argument here) would discard the validation that rejects a serialized signature-slot count disagreeing with the message header's required-signature count, and a signature-count prefix longer than one byte, before any `createTransaction` builds a mutable `TransactionRecord`. Dropping the argument also invalidates the `@throws IllegalStateException` Javadoc that hunks 2 and 7 keep on the three abstract `createTransaction` declarations.

instructions.question: How does the defect described by `b` relate to the defect described by `a`?
instructions.focus: Compare the defects, not the wording. Two findings about the same code can still be different defects.

criteria: Different defects: fixing the defect `a` describes would leave the defect `b` describes unfixed, even when both sit in the same code.
The same underlying defect, but `b` narrows it, re-scopes which instances or inputs it covers, or reports it at a different place. Not a different defect in adjacent code.
The same defect restated in different words: fixing one fixes the other.

claims_new_evidence.instructions: Does `b` cite evidence that `a` does not?

criteria.true: `b` names a file, test, command, observation, or reproduction that `a` does not mention.
criteria.false: `b` cites nothing beyond what `a` already cites, or cites nothing at all.
